files.lesson.md: --- order: 31 unit: error9 node: AC9M9M04 n1 uses: [AC9M9M02 n1] assumes: [AC9M8M01 n1] connection: part-tolerance title: Every measurement is an estimate summary: "A reading to the nearest millimetre could be up to half a millimetre out either way. The true value is somewhere between a lower bound and an upper bound." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A bolt hole must be 20 mm, give or take 0.05 mm. A measured hole is 20.04 mm. Does it pass?" --- A factory makes a bolt hole that must be 20 mm, give or take 0.05 mm. An inspector measures one and gets 20.04 mm. Does it pass? Have a guess, and we'll come back to it at the end. (The numbers are made up for the task.) ## Predict: how far out ```step stage: predict insight: "Choosing the range for a 24 mm reading shows whether students treat a reading as exact or as the nearest mark." check: type: predict q: "A ruler with marks every 1 mm reads 24 mm for a length. What could the true length be?" options: - "Anything from 23.5 mm to 24.5 mm" - "Exactly 24 mm" - "Anything from 24 mm to 25 mm" - "Anything from 23 mm to 25 mm" actual: "Anything from 23.5 mm to 24.5 mm. The reading is the nearest mark, so the true length is within half a millimetre of 24 either way." ``` ## Run: the bounds ```step stage: run insight: "The reading plus or minus half of the smallest mark gives the upper and lower bounds." check: { type: number, q: "A ruler reads $24$ mm to the nearest mm. What is the lower bound? (mm)", answer: 23.5, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "24 − 0.5 = 23.5 mm." } ``` ## Investigate: half the precision ```step stage: investigate insight: "The bounds are half the smallest unit either side. A reading is never exact, only closest." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A tape reads $156$ cm to the nearest cm. What is the upper bound? (cm)" answer: 156.5 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "156 + 0.5 = 156.5 cm." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is half of 1 cm? (cm)", answer: 0.5, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "Half of 1 is 0.5." } - check: type: number q: "A scale reads $3.2$ kg to the nearest $0.1$ kg. What is the upper bound? (kg)" answer: 3.25 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "Half of 0.1 is 0.05, so 3.2 + 0.05 = 3.25 kg." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#max" text: "Max checks a bolt measured to the nearest millimetre. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: measurement-exact explain: "Line 2: a reading of 20 mm to the nearest mm only says the true value is between 19.5 and 20.5 mm." ``` ### Bounds ```worked \text{reading } 24 \text{ mm, to the nearest } 1 \text{ mm} :: The smallest mark is 1 mm. 1 \div 2 = 0.5 :: Half the smallest mark. 24 - 0.5 = 23.5 :: Lower bound. 24 + 0.5 = 24.5 :: Upper bound. 23.5 \le \text{true length} < 24.5 :: The true value is in this range. ``` ### Half the mark ### Find the mistake Read Max's working. Which line treats the reading as exact? ## Modify: change the instrument ```step stage: modify insight: "A finer instrument has narrower bounds, but never none." tasks: - hint: ["The smallest mark is 0.01 mm.", "Half of that is 0.005."] check: { type: number, q: "Calipers read $20.04$ mm to the nearest $0.01$ mm. What is the upper bound? (mm)", answer: 20.045, tolerance: 0.0005, explain: "20.04 + 0.005 = 20.045 mm." } - hint: ["The part passes if it's between 19.95 and 20.05.", "Is the upper bound inside?"] check: { type: question, q: "The hole must be $20$ mm give or take $0.05$ mm ($19.95$ to $20.05$). The calipers read $20.04$ mm (bounds $20.035$ to $20.045$). Does it pass?", options: ["Yes: the whole range is inside the tolerance", "No: 20.04 is too big", "Only if it's exactly 20", "Can't tell"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "20.04 is less than 20.05.", "Nothing is exactly 20 in measurement.", "You can tell: both bounds are inside."], explain: "Both 20.035 and 20.045 are between 19.95 and 20.05, so it passes." } - hint: ["Compute the upper bound for 20.05.", "20.05 + 0.005."] check: { type: question, q: "A second hole reads $20.05$ mm on the same calipers. Does it pass for sure?", options: ["No: its upper bound is 20.055, above the 20.05 limit, so it might fail", "Yes: 20.05 is exactly the limit", "Yes: it is under 20.1", "No: it is exactly 20.05"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "The true value could be a little above the limit.", "The limit is 20.05, not 20.1.", "Reading isn't exact: the true value may be less."], explain: "The reading is 20.05 but the true value could be up to 20.055, so you can't be certain." } ``` ### Upper bound ### Does it pass ### On the limit ## Practise: bounds ```step stage: practise insight: "Finding both bounds from a reading and its precision." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A reading is 12 cm to the nearest cm. What is the lower bound? (cm)" answer: 11.5 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "12 − 0.5 = 11.5." - check: type: number q: "A reading is 4.6 s to the nearest 0.1 s. What is the upper bound? (s)" answer: 4.65 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "4.6 + 0.05 = 4.65." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is half of 0.1?", answer: 0.05, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "Half of 0.1 is 0.05." } - check: type: number q: "Review: a shape's side is 5 cm. It is enlarged with a scale factor of 3. What is the new area if the original area was 4 cm²? (cm²)" answer: 36 explain: "4 × 3² = 36." ``` ### Lower bound ### Upper bound ### Review ## Make: does it pass ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the bolt hole: both bounds must sit inside the tolerance for the part to pass for sure." tasks: - hint: ["Half of 0.01 is 0.005.", "Compare the bounds with 19.95 and 20.05."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A hole must be 20 mm give or take 0.05 mm. The calipers read 20.04 mm to the nearest 0.01 mm. What is the upper bound of the true diameter? (mm; made up for the task)" steps: - ["precision $0.01$, half is $0.005$", "half the smallest mark"] - ["upper bound $= 20.04 + 0.005 = 20.045$", "add"] - ["$20.045 < 20.05$, so it passes", "inside the limit"] answer: "20.045" answerLabel: "Upper bound (mm)" tolerance: 0.0005 feedback: - ["20.04", "That's the reading. Add half the smallest mark."] - ["20.05", "That's the tolerance limit. Find the upper bound of the reading."] criteria: - "I halved the precision." - "I added it to the reading." - "I compared with the limit." explain: "20.04 + 0.005 = 20.045 mm, below 20.05 mm, so the part passes." - check: type: question q: "Why does a good inspector care about the instrument's precision as well as the reading?" options: ["The bounds decide whether you can be sure the part passes", "Precision doesn't matter", "Readings are always exact", "Only the limit matters"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "It can change the decision.", "Every measurement is an estimate.", "Both matter."] explain: "The same reading could pass with fine calipers and be uncertain with a coarse ruler." ``` ### The upper bound ### Why precision matters **Also used in** - **Manufacturing.** Parts are made to a tolerance and checked with calibrated instruments. - **Science.** Every result has an uncertainty, and good reports give it. - **Next lesson.** How big the error is, and how it compares. ```teacher summary: Students find the lower and upper bounds of a measurement from its precision (AC9M9M04, node 1). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 6 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 11 min goals: - I can say why a measurement is only an estimate. - I can find the bounds from a reading and its precision. - I can decide if a part passes a tolerance. struggle: "Thinking a reading is exact. Ask: could the true length be a bit more than the nearest mark?" before: > Students need Scientific notation and decimals. The one idea: half the smallest mark either side. A measured value alone is not the whole story. The bolt hole numbers are made up for the task. Have rulers and a stopwatch so students can measure something. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check." - "Paper: the upper bound in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student gives the bounds as ±1 unit. ask: How far could a reading be from the true value if it is the nearest mark? fix: Half a mark. stretch: Measure a desk with a ruler marked in cm and mm and compare the bounds. support: A printed ruler with bounds shaded. leads: | Continues AC9M9M04 node 1. Where it leads: Absolute and relative error. exit: q: A reading is 7 cm to the nearest cm. What are the bounds? a: 6.5 cm and 7.5 cm. explain: | A reading to the nearest mark could be half a mark out either way. The true value is between the lower and the upper bound. ```
